extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry / readers of Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and structural facts for recognizing and manipulating important properties of morphisms of schemes (separatedness, quasiseparatedness, properness, projectivity, graphs, rational maps, and dimension). Useful for proving that a morphism has a given property or for reasoning about when two morphisms agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiseparated is local on the target
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that the condition of being quasiseparated is local on the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: the condition of being quasicompact is local on the target (Exercise 7.3.C(a)); use a similar argument as in Proposition 10.1.11. (This is presented as Exercise 10.1.I.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Separatedness closed under composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The condition of being separated is closed under composition: if π:X→Y and ρ:Y→Z are separated, then ρ◦π:X→Z is separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the magic Cartesian diagram (Exercise 1.3.S) and the fact that closed embeddings are preserved by base change and composition; i.e., the diagonal of the composite is a composition of closed embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiseparated closed under composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The condition of being quasiseparated is closed under composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same argument as for separatedness but with “closed embedding” replaced by “quasicompact”. (Proposition 10.1.13(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiprojective implies separated
rubrics_metrics.description: Every quasiprojective A-scheme is separated over A. In particular, every reduced quasiprojective k-scheme is a k-variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure morphism of a quasiprojective scheme factors as an open embedding followed by a closed embedding into P^n_A; open and closed embeddings and P^n_A are separated, and separatedness is preserved under composition (Corollary 10.1.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product of separated/quasiseparated morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If π:X→Y and π':X'→Y' are separated (resp. quasiseparated) S-morphisms, then the product morphism π×_S π':X×_S X' → Y×_S Y' is separated (resp. quasiseparated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard fibered-product exercises (Exercise 9.4.F); property is preserved under products (Proposition 10.1.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph morphism properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For π:X→Y (over Z), the graph morphism Γ_π:X→X×_Z Y given by (id,π) is called the graph; Γ_π is always a locally closed embedding. If Y is separated over Z, Γ_π is a closed embedding. If Y is quasiseparated over Z, Γ_π is quasicompact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the special case of the magic diagram (Exercise 1.3.S). The properties (locally closed embedding, closed embedding, quasicompact) are preserved under base change, so they lift from the diagonal δ:Y→Y×_Z Y to Γ_π (Proposition 10.1.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation Theorem for a property P of morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be a class of morphisms preserved by base change and composition. In a commutative diagram with maps τ, π, ρ, if certain arrows are in P and the diagonal δ_ρ:Y→Y×_Z Y is in P (or satisfies related hypotheses), then π is in P. Special consequences: (i) if locally closed embeddings are in P, then τ∈P ⇒ π∈P. (ii) if closed embeddings are in P, then τ∈P and ρ separated ⇒ π∈P. (iii) if quasicompact morphisms are in P, then τ∈P and ρ quasiseparated ⇒ π∈P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses the graph Cartesian diagram and base-change preservation of P; plug in different P to get many useful nonobvious consequences (Proposition 10.1.19). Examples: injectivity/surjectivity analogues in Sets are illuminating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus where two morphisms agree is a largest locally closed subscheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two morphisms π,π':X→Y over Z, there is a largest locally closed subscheme V⊂X on which π and π' agree; if Y is separated over Z then V is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define V as the fibered product along the diagonal (π,π'):X→Y and δ:Y→Y×_Z Y. Since δ is a locally closed (resp. closed) embedding, V is locally closed (resp. closed); V has the universal property: any µ:W→X on which π◦µ=π'◦µ factors uniquely through V (Exercise 10.2.A and minor remarks). Note locus can be nonreduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced-to-Separated Theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: Two S-morphisms π,π':U→Z from a reduced scheme U to a separated S-scheme Z that agree on a dense open subset of U must be equal on all of U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let V be the (closed) locus where π and π' agree; it contains a dense open subset and therefore equals U because U is reduced. Consequences: rational maps from reduced sources to separated targets have a largest domain of definition, rational functions on reduced schemes have largest domains, etc. (Theorem 10.2.2.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph of a rational map: definition and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is reduced and Y separated, the graph Γ_π of a rational map π:X  -⇢ Y is defined as the scheme-theoretic closure of Γ_{π'} inside X×Y for any representative π':U→Y; this closure is independent of the representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take any representative (U,π') with π' a morphism on open U. Γ_{π'} is a closed embedding composed with an open embedding; take closure in X×Y. Independence of representative is shown by reducing to V the domain of definition and using Reduced-to-Separated and scheme-theoretic closure arguments (10.2.4 and Exercise 10.2.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper morphism (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π:X→Y is proper if it is separated, of finite type, and universally closed. A scheme X is proper over A if the structure morphism X→Spec A is proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universal closedness means the morphism remains closed under any base change. Properness is the scheme-theoretic analogue of compactness for varieties (Definition 10.3.1). Examples and nonexamples are used to illustrate the importance of the universal condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed embeddings are proper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closed embeddings are separated and finite type; after base change they remain closed embeddings, hence remain closed maps; hence they satisfy the definition of proper (Example 10.3.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite morphisms are proper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finite morphisms are affine (hence separated), finite type, and remain finite (hence closed) after any base change; hence they are proper (Proposition 10.3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective schemes are proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Projective A-schemes are proper over A (Theorem 10.3.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor the structure morphism as a closed embedding into P^n_A followed by projection; closed embeddings are proper and P^n_A→Spec A is shown to be universally closed using elimination theory (Fundamental Theorem of Elimination Theory / Theorem 7.4.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal properties of proper morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Properness is stable under base change, is local on the target, closed under composition, products of proper morphisms are proper, and cancellation: if τ is proper and ρ is separated in a commutative diagram, then π is proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each property follows because separatedness, finite type, and universal closedness are all preserved by base change and composition; use the Cancellation Theorem for proper morphisms where needed (Proposition 10.3.4 and applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constancy of functions on connected reduced proper k-schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a connected, reduced, proper k-scheme where k is algebraically closed, then Γ(X,O_X)=k: every global regular function is constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret a function as a morphism X→A^1; extend to P^1 and use properness to show image must be a point; scheme-theoretic image arguments complete the proof (10.3.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness facts (sketch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finiteness characterizations: a morphism is finite iff it is proper and affine; equivalently, finite iff proper and quasi-finite (Theorem 29.6.2; proof deferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives practical consequences: quasi-finite morphisms from proper schemes to separated schemes are finite (discussion in 10.3.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigidity Lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be proper, Y geometrically integral with a rational point p and irreducible, and Z any variety. If α:X×Y→Z is a morphism constant on X×{q} for some q∈Y, then α factors through Y (i.e., α = ψ∘pr for some ψ:Y→Z). If α is also constant on {p}×Y, then α is constant on all of X×Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to showing α equals the function β(x,y)=α(p,y) on a dense open subset using properness and base change arguments; uses that fibers over geometric points map to points and Exercise 10.2.B (maps determined by closed points over alg. closed fields) (Lemma/Theorem 10.3.12). Consequence: morphisms from abelian varieties to group varieties are translation composed with a homomorphism; abelian varieties are commutative (Corollary 10.3.13 and exercises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of dimension (Krull dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dimension of a topological space X is the supremum of lengths of chains of closed irreducible subsets (indexing starts at 0). Dimension of a ring is the supremum of lengths of chains of nested prime ideals. (Empty set has dimension −∞.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This topological/Krull definition is used for schemes: dim Spec A = dim A (Exercise 11.1.A). Examples: dim A^1_k = 1, dim Spec Z = 1, dim Spec k = 0, dim Spec k[x]/(x^2) = 0. Remarks emphasize subtlety and topological nature of dimension (Section 11.1.1 and 11.1.2).
